title: The Last Oath Anew
premise: Felix Yarrow has spent her life in Thornvale, the one valley where oath-magic cannot follow, hiding the fact that she is the last swordspeaker—a person whose spoken vows can bind reality itself. When a dying courier gives her a map to the Undercourt, where souls are traded like coin, she learns her own mother's soul was sold there twenty years ago, and the buyer intends to use it to unmake the valley's protection. Guided by a disgraced oathbreaker knight and a thief who remembers nothing of her own past, Felix descends beneath the mountain, discovering that her invisibility was a cage built by the very court she must rob. To free her mother's soul, Felix must swear a new oath that will either restore her stolen identity or erase her from memory entirely—and in the end she chooses to bind herself to her found family, sacrificing the last of her old life to bring everyone home.
about_author: Kestrel Voss is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval oath documents before turning to fiction, and her love of legal language and old magic saturates every page. She writes from a cluttered cottage in the Pacific Northwest, where she is rarely seen without a dog and an unfinished draft.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Felix Yarrow's POV. We meet Thornvale, where magic dies at the tree line, and Felix, who sharpens ordinary blades and hides her gift for spoken oaths. When a stranger stumbles into her smithy bleeding and whispering about the Undercourt, she wants only to send him away. Beat: the quiet dread of a life built on concealment cracking open.

chapters.title: A Map in Dying Hands
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The courier, Merrin, dies on her floor, pressing a bloodstained map into her grip and gasping that 'the Yarrow soul is called due.' The map burns when she tries to burn it. Beat: reluctant inheritance—the moment staying invisible stops being an option.

chapters.title: What the Elders Buried
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She confronts the valley matriarch, Odile, who admits her mother's soul was sold to buy Thornvale's protection—and that Felix was the price's collateral. Odile orders her to destroy the map. Beat: betrayal by the guardians of her childhood; the first fracture in her identity.

chapters.title: The Oathbreaker at the Gate
chapters.summary: Sir Aldric Vane's POV. A disgraced knight arrives seeking the last swordspeaker to break the oath that chains him. Felix refuses, but he recognizes her mother's sigil on the map and offers passage instead. Beat: wary alliance; two people defined by oaths they never chose.

chapters.title: The Thief with No Yesterday
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A quick-fingered thief joins them at the border inn—she remembers nothing before three years ago, only that the Undercourt took her memories as payment. She can read the map's cipher. Beat: found family's first stitch; humor and hunger at a shared table.

chapters.title: Crossing the Tree Line
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. They leave the valley; magic floods back into Felix like cold water, and her suppressed oaths begin whispering in her blood. The first night outside, she speaks a small vow and a river holds still for her. Beat: awe and terror of a self she's never been allowed to be.

chapters.title: The Toll of Names
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At a border market, a soul-broker recognizes the map and offers to buy 'the empty girl' back from the court. Wren refuses, shaken; Felix learns Wren's memories were sold to someone specific. Beat: the market's casual cruelty; Wren's fear that her past is worse than her blanks.

chapters.title: Aldric's Broken Vow
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. Around the fire, Aldric confesses he swore to protect a prince and watched him die instead—an oath that now flays him nightly. He believes only a swordspeaker can release him. Beat: guilt made flesh; the cost of promises kept too literally.

chapters.title: The Mountain's Mouth
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. They reach the Undercourt's gate, a cave mouth that speaks their names back to them in dead voices—including Felix's mother's. The gate demands an oath of entry: each must name what they'll surrender. Beat: threshold dread; the price of descent made explicit.

chapters.title: Streets of Sold Things
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Inside the Undercourt, a cavern city of lantern-lit markets where memories, years, and names are traded. Wren finds a stall selling fragments of her own childhood and buys one: a woman's voice singing. Beat: longing and grief; the first taste of a stolen self.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Yarrow
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. In the court's archive, Felix finds her mother's soul recorded as collateral on a debt Odile never paid—and the debt's holder is the Undercourt's Regent, who plans to use a Yarrow soul to unravel the valley's ward and claim the magic-dead land. Beat: the stakes sharpen from personal to catastrophic.

chapters.title: An Audience of Masks
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Brought before the Regent, who wears a mask of her mother's face, Felix is offered a trade: her mother's freedom for her own soul, 'the last oath-bound one.' She stalls, swearing a false oath she doesn't intend to keep—and the court's magic marks her for perjury. Beat: the seduction of a terrible bargain; a lie with a timer on it.

chapters.title: What Wren Remembered
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The bought memory blooms: Wren was the Regent's own daughter, her memory sold to hide the Regent's one act of mercy—freeing a Yarrow child from the ledger years ago. Beat: devastating reversal; Wren realizes her found family was written into her before she met them.

chapters.title: Perjury's Price
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. The false oath begins to consume Felix—her reflection fades, her name slips from strangers' tongues. Aldric, who knows what broken oaths do, teaches her to anchor herself by speaking true vows aloud each dawn. Beat: ticking-clock tension; identity eroding in real time.

chapters.title: The Vault Beneath the Court
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. With Wren's insider knowledge, the trio infiltrates the soul-vault, a cathedral of glass jars each holding a murmuring life. Felix finds her mother's jar—warm, humming the song from Wren's memory. Beat: hope at its most fragile; the heist's quiet center.

chapters.title: Betrayal in Glass
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. The Regent anticipated them: Aldric's old oath to the crown activates—he was sent to deliver a swordspeaker all along. In agony, he turns on Felix, shattering the vault's wards. Beat: the lowest moment; loyalty versus compulsion, and the vault's alarms waking the court.

chapters.title: Every Oath at Once
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Hunted through the cavern city, Felix realizes she cannot outfight the court—only out-speak it. She begins unbinding Aldric's compulsion with a counter-oath, pouring her fading name into the words. Beat: the swordspeaker's gift fully awakened; sacrifice as weapon.

chapters.title: The Regent Unmasked
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Confronting the Regent, Felix tears the mask away: beneath is her mother—not a soul in a jar, but a woman remade into the court's instrument. The Regent's plan was to send a Yarrow soul home as a Trojan horse to break the valley's ward. Beat: climax's emotional peak; the enemy wears a beloved face.

chapters.title: The Last Oath Anew
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix cannot free her mother without fulfilling the Regent's design, so she swears a new oath—not to blood, but to Aldric and Wren—binding her soul to her found family, making it worthless as collateral and shattering the ledger's claim. The court's magic recoils; her mother's true self flickers free. Beat: climax; identity chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: The Mountain Comes Down
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. The broken ledger unbinds every sold soul; the Undercourt collapses as its economy of selves fails. The trio flees upward through falling stone, carrying Wren's recovered memories and a mother who no longer knows her daughter's name. Beat: escape amid ruin; cost tallied in what can't be restored.

chapters.title: Home, Rewritten
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. They reach Thornvale, where the ward holds—strengthened, ironically, by the debt's dissolution. Felix's mother begins again as a stranger among kind faces; Odile kneels in penance. Wren chooses to stay with the family she found twice. Beat: bittersweet resolution; found family as the true inheritance.

chapters.title: The Smithy at the Tree Line
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A year later, Felix forges blades by day and teaches Wren to speak small true oaths by night; Aldric repairs the valley's old watchtower. Her mother tends the garden, learning to love a daughter she doesn't remember. Felix swears one final quiet vow to no power at all—just to stay. Beat: peace earned, identity whole, the door left open.
